headline: When the Coding Agent Becomes the Video Director
lede: Most AI video tools ask a neural network to conjure footage from nothing. Remotion, a three-person Swiss company, is betting on a different premise: that the most useful AI-produced video is not generated pixel by pixel but written — as React code — by a coding agent that has been taught the rules of the framework. Their new **Agent Skills** integration makes that possible directly inside Claude Code, Codex, and a dozen other agentic tools.
body:
Remotion's core proposition is that video is a rendering problem, not a generation problem. Founded by Jonny Burger in February 2021 and incorporated as **Remotion AG** in Zurich, the framework lets developers write React components where time is a variable: a `frame` prop counts up from zero, and standard JavaScript interpolation governs motion, opacity, scale, and sequencing. A *headless-Chrome* pipeline renders those components into MP4. The output is deterministic and version-controlled — the same source code produces the same video, every time. By May 2026, the project has accumulated roughly 46,000 GitHub stars and claims to render more than one million videos per month for over 200 enterprise customers.

The new integration rides an open standard that Anthropic published in December 2025. *Agent Skills* are not *MCP* (Model Context Protocol) — Anthropic's earlier, heavier standard for giving agents live access to tools via JSON-RPC servers. They are simpler: a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter and Markdown instructions, distributed via a single `npx skills add` command. A *progressive-disclosure architecture* keeps context lean: skill metadata (roughly 100 tokens) loads at agent startup; the full instruction body loads only when a task matches the skill's domain; referenced sub-files arrive on demand. The standard has since been adopted across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and others.

What the Remotion skill installs is 28 modular rule files covering component patterns, animation primitives, transition types, audio integration, caption generation, Three.js 3D rendering, and Lambda deployment. When a user prompts Claude Code to make a product launch video, the agent pulls in the relevant rule files and writes syntactically correct Remotion code — *spring-physics* configs, interpolation ranges, sequence nesting — without hallucinating the framework's API. The agent then executes the render locally or via Remotion's cloud infrastructure. No generative-video model is involved; the “AI” in the loop is the coding agent, and the “video” is compiled React.

This puts Remotion in a distinct competitive position relative to tools like Sora, Runway, or Veo — none of which it is trying to replace. Generative video excels at stochastic, photorealistic footage where no two renders are identical; code-driven video excels at reproducibility, templating, and high-volume variants — a hundred localized ad cuts from a single base component, for instance. The closer comparisons are Motion Canvas, Revideo, and Manim, all of which address programmatic animation but lack Remotion's commercial infrastructure and, now, its agentic distribution reach.

Remotion AG remains determinedly small. Burger and business co-founder Mehmet Ademi have raised a total of CHF 241,000 from roughly fourteen angel investors, all described on the company's own investor page as Remotion users or customers. The documentation states the company is “not looking to raise any more funding” and turned slightly profitable in 2024. It is private, not publicly traded, and incorporated as an *Aktiengesellschaft* — the Swiss equivalent of a joint-stock company — in Zurich.

concepts.definition: An open standard published by Anthropic in December 2025 for packaging domain knowledge into lightweight SKILL.md text files that AI coding agents load as context. Skills are installed via a single `npx skills add` command and work across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agents. Unlike MCP, they are purely instructional — no servers, no API calls, no authentication.

Anthropic's earlier standard for giving AI agents live access to external tools — databases, APIs, file systems — via JSON-RPC servers. Requires running server processes and, often, OAuth credentials. Agent Skills are the simpler, documentation-only alternative for context injection rather than tool execution.

In the Agent Skills protocol, a three-layer loading scheme: skill metadata (~100 tokens) loads at agent startup; the full SKILL.md instruction body loads when a task matches the skill's domain; referenced sub-files load on demand. The design keeps the agent's context window lean while preserving access to deep specifics.

A mode of the Google Chrome browser that runs without a graphical interface and is controllable programmatically. Remotion uses it to render React components — including their time-based animation logic — into individual video frames, which are then stitched into an MP4 file.

Video whose output is fully reproducible from its source code: the same input always produces the same frames. Contrasts with generative AI video (Sora, Runway), where two runs of the same prompt yield different footage. Enables version control, templating, and mass localization at scale.

An animation model that mimics the behavior of a physical spring — overshoot, settle, and damping — to produce motion that feels natural rather than mechanical. Remotion exposes a `spring()` function that takes stiffness and damping parameters and returns an interpolated value for any given frame number.

The German and Swiss term for a joint-stock company (abbreviated AG), roughly equivalent to a public limited company in the UK or a C-corporation in the US. Despite the corporate form, Remotion AG is private — the designation refers to its legal structure, not its listing status.

repos.summary: The main Remotion repository: a TypeScript framework for creating videos with React, rendered via headless Chrome. Source-available under a proprietary license (free for individuals and companies under three employees). Roughly 46,000 GitHub stars as of May 2026.

Remotion's Agent Skills package — 28 SKILL.md rule files covering components, animations, transitions, audio, captions, 3D rendering, and deployment. Installed via `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills`, it teaches coding agents like Claude Code and Codex to write valid Remotion code without hallucinating the framework's API.
